introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Pure Mathematics with Mechanics Paper 2 (0765/2), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2023. Time allowed: three hours.**

Full marks may be obtained for answers to ALL questions. Mathematical formulae booklets published by the GCE Board are allowed. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving the answer at each stage. Calculators are allowed. Start each question on a fresh page.

questions.enonce_markdown: Given that $f(x) = \sin x \ln(\tan x)$, find $f'(x)$ when $x = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$. (5 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
Use the product rule with $u = \sin x$ and $v = \ln(\tan x)$.

$$u' = \cos x, \qquad v' = \frac{1}{\tan x}\cdot\frac{d}{dx}(\tan x) = \frac{\sec^2 x}{\tan x}.$$

Simplify $v'$: $\dfrac{\sec^2 x}{\tan x} = \dfrac{1/\cos^2 x}{\sin x/\cos x} = \dfrac{1}{\sin x\cos x}$.

$$f'(x) = u'v + uv' = \cos x\,\ln(\tan x) + \sin x\cdot\frac{1}{\sin x\cos x} = \cos x\,\ln(\tan x) + \frac{1}{\cos x}.$$

At $x = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$: $\tan\dfrac{\pi}{4} = 1$, so $\ln\left(\tan\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = \ln 1 = 0$, and $\cos\dfrac{\pi}{4} = \dfrac{\sqrt2}{2}$.

$$f'\!\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right) = \frac{\sqrt2}{2}\times 0 + \frac{1}{\sqrt2/2} = \frac{2}{\sqrt2} = \sqrt2.$$

$$\boxed{f'\!\left(\tfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = \sqrt2 \approx 1.414}$$

questions.enonce_markdown: Evaluate $\displaystyle\int_2^{10} \frac{x}{\sqrt{x-1}}\,dx$, using the substitution $u^2 = x - 1$. (5 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
Let $u^2 = x - 1$, with $u > 0$ (so $u = \sqrt{x-1}$). Then

$$x = u^2 + 1, \qquad 2u\,du = dx, \qquad \sqrt{x-1} = u.$$

Change the limits: when $x = 2$, $u^2 = 1$, so $u = 1$; when $x = 10$, $u^2 = 9$, so $u = 3$.

$$\int_2^{10}\frac{x}{\sqrt{x-1}}\,dx = \int_1^3 \frac{u^2 + 1}{u}\cdot 2u\,du = 2\int_1^3 (u^2 + 1)\,du = 2\left[\frac{u^3}{3} + u\right]_1^3.$$

$$= 2\left[(9 + 3) - \left(\frac13 + 1\right)\right] = 2\left[12 - \frac43\right] = 2\times\frac{32}{3} = \frac{64}{3}.$$

$$\boxed{\int_2^{10}\frac{x}{\sqrt{x-1}}\,dx = \frac{64}{3} \approx 21.33}$$

(A numerical integration of the original integral gives $21.3333$, which confirms the result.)
